newsitem.title: POLAND: Union tells Polish left to consult on constitution.
newsitem.headline: Union tells Polish left to consult on constitution.

text.p: The head of Poland's Solidarity trade union warned the ruling ex-communists on Thursday not to pass a new national constitution without heeding a draft submitted by the extra-parliamentary opposition.
"This...could be a very dangerous legal measure for Poland which could destabilise the situation," Marian Krzaklewski told a news conference after talks with parliament speaker Jozef Zych.

The union has grouped centre-right parties in a new Solidarity Election Action (AWS) which has little support in the current parliament but rivals the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) for first place in opinion polls.
The ex-communists, dominant force in the ruling coalition, are completing work on a new constitution to replace a 1952 charter rendered obsolete by the 1989 fall of communism.
They hope to put it to a referendum before or during coming parliamentary polls due late this year.
Krzaklewski said parliament's constitutional committee had paid little heed to a draft backed by Solidarity and signed by two million voters that was submitted two years ago.
"Therefore the fear arises that the draft that is passed could be confrontational to a significant part of the electorate," the Solidarity president said.
He said the current left-dominated parliament had been elected in 1993 and should not be the exclusive author of a constitution in 1997, when the political balance had changed.
He called for more consultation outside parliament and suggested a version unacceptable to the union could be blocked by Solidarity supporters in the referendum.

The strongly-Catholic Solidarity wants a constitution founded on natural law rather than purely secular principles, that would offer social guarantees, favour families and give unions a say in the workplace and in preparing legislation. @
